findings.title: C12's four escape-class checks are not FR-D8's four classes
findings.body: Spec B FR-D8's four-class check is: unrun review; same-family seat; unfetched findings (a seat's result never landed, including reconciliation failures); and disposition without a receipt on the head (false convergence). C12's What instead names 'unrun review …, same-family seat, unfetched fix verification, stale or unbound evidence'. That replaces unfetched findings and disposition-without-receipt with two other predicates. The six cases later in the same What still use the spec's tokens ('unfetched findings', 'disposition without a receipt'), so the child contradicts both the spec and itself. A builder following the parenthetical four-check list would not implement FR-D1/FR-D8 class four, and C12's DoD never grades a same-family refusal at all.
findings.suggestion: Name the four checks exactly as FR-D8.7: unrun review, same-family seat, unfetched findings, disposition without a receipt on the head. Keep stale-head as the qualifying-result rule inside unrun review / the six cases, not as a fourth class. Add a DoD dry-run that a same-family panel refuses, naming that class.
findings.evidence: Spec B FR-D8.7: 'unrun review …; same-family seat …; unfetched findings (a seat's result never landed in the record, including the reconciliation failures above); disposition without a receipt on the head …'. C12.md line 3: 'runs the four escape-class checks (unrun review by engagement telemetry …, same-family seat, unfetched fix verification, stale or unbound evidence)'.

findings.title: C12 quotes R26 and owns FR-M7.2 but neither is in the DoD
findings.body: C12 consumes R26 and the coverage map gives it FR-M7.2 (class-coverage re-checked at the child's build head, result recorded in the D1 annex coverage-check section with date and head) and FR-M1.7's live-declaration move for the D1 surface. The DoD grades the writer boundary, the six cases, R5 fields, specimens, baselines, the bump, and the no-trigger refusal. It does not require a dated annex closing note, a live-declaration move into the writer/envelope home, or a recorded class-coverage run. C10 and C13 grade their closing notes; C12, which owns most D1 rows, does not. A vet could merge C12 with no annex re-verification.
findings.suggestion: Add DoD bullets: (1) D1 live declaration moved into the writer/envelope home, with a dated closing note per row this child touched and the table's last correction; (2) FR-D1 class-coverage re-run at this head, result in the annex coverage-check section with date and head, no class left without a preventer.
findings.evidence: R26: 'Each of C10, C11, C12, and C13 moves the live declaration of its surface into the implementation home … re-verifies its rows against its build head with a dated note, and writes the table's last correction in its closing note.' Spec B FR-M7.2: 'FR-D1's class-coverage rule … is checked … again at each child's build head … Each run records its result in the D1 annex's coverage-check section with the date and head.' C12.md DoD lines 6–13 contain neither artifact.

findings.title: C12's must-refuse DoD does not grade FR-D2's three counter-specimen shapes
findings.body: Spec B FR-D2.2 requires the paired counter-specimen to refuse in three shapes: bare fabricated findings files; a well-formed hand-landed envelope over fabricated findings (correct hash, correct anchor); and a caller-supplied file placed in the execution-evidence slot itself. C12 owns that bullet. What only says 'the fixture pair re-cut and both specimens kept'. The DoD says 'the must-refuse counter-specimens refuse' with no list of shapes and no requirement that the refusal name the class and missing artifact. The third shape is the discriminator mutant; a vet cannot tell from the DoD whether it was exercised.
findings.suggestion: Enumerate the three FR-D2.2 shapes in What and DoD. Require each recorded refusal to name the FR-D1 class and the missing or unauthenticatable artifact.
findings.evidence: Spec B FR-D2.2: 'seat outputs authored but never executed must still refuse, in three shapes. First, bare fabricated findings files. Second, a well-formed hand-landed envelope over fabricated findings … Third, a caller-supplied file placed in the execution-evidence slot itself.' C12.md line 9: 'the must-refuse counter-specimens refuse'.

findings.title: C12's baseline record drops FR-D3.1's weekly-eats corroboration and fail-toward-alerting path
findings.body: Spec B FR-D3.1 requires the pre-shrink baseline (certified-loop completion over this repo's trailing ten full lanes) and, beside it, the weekly-eats figure (2 of 5) as consumer corroboration never mixed into the denominator; if the records cannot produce the number, any post-shrink silent certified-loop drop-off observed at a driver-surface vet counts as a firing. C12's What records only 'certified-loop completion over the trailing ten full lanes; the driver-core fix share'. The DoD asks for 'pre-shrink baselines … with the records they were read from' and does not mention the 2-of-5 figure or the fail-toward-alerting substitute. C12 owns FR-D3.1.
findings.suggestion: In What and DoD, require the V-1 baseline, the weekly-eats 2-of-5 recorded beside it and not in the denominator, and an explicit annex note of either the computed number or that records could not produce it and the silent-drop-off firing rule is in force.
findings.evidence: Spec B FR-D3.1: 'The weekly-eats figure (2 of 5 full lanes completing certified …) is recorded beside it as consumer corroboration, never mixed into the denominator. If the records cannot produce the number, the comparator fails toward alerting: any post-shrink silent certified-loop drop-off … counts as a firing.' C12.md line 3: 'the advisor records the pre-shrink baselines (certified-loop completion over the trailing ten full lanes; the driver-core fix share)'.

findings.title: C15 treats own-worktree retirement as deleting doc lines the spec keeps
findings.body: Spec A FR-B6 and R15 retire only the launcher-enforced half of the own-worktree ruling; 'the prose stays for direct builders'. C15's What repeats that parenthetical, then says each of the six pieces leaves 'with its tests and doc lines'. The DoD defines deleted as 'module, tests, and doc lines gone' for every piece, with no exception for the staying prose. A not-needed receipt line plus that DoD would delete the direct-builder rule.
findings.suggestion: Split the own-worktree outcome: launcher enforcement and its tests may go when the receipt says not-needed; the direct-builder prose is listed as remaining. Do not use 'doc lines gone' as the delete definition for that piece.
findings.evidence: Spec A FR-B6.2 / R15: 'the launcher-enforced half of the own-worktree ruling (the prose stays for direct builders)'. C15.md line 6: 'deleted (module, tests, and doc lines gone)'.

findings.title: C15 does not grade the staying launch ledger and rulings block; the quota grep fights them
findings.body: R15 and Spec A FR-B6 say the launch ledger and the launch doctrine's rulings block are doctrine and stay. C15's What repeats that. No DoD bullet requires those files to remain. The quota DoD instead requires a grep for 'quota' under plugins/superheroes (excluding docs/ and decomposition artifacts) to return only the parked poller and the glossary history note. A staying rulings block that records the 2026-09-05 quota ruling, or C4's quota prose lines in plugin-tree files, would fail that grep. A vet cannot pass both 'rulings block stays' and 'no quota string except poller and glossary'.
findings.suggestion: Add a DoD bullet that the launch ledger and the launch doctrine rulings block are present after the merge. Narrow the quota grep to the removed surfaces (preflight check one, quota leg, suspect-quota recovery, their tests), and allow doctrine that records the retirement ruling.
findings.evidence: R15: 'The launch ledger and the launch doctrine's rulings block are doctrine, not workarounds, and stay.' C15.md line 8: 'a grep for quota over plugins/superheroes (excluding docs/ and the decomposition artifacts) returns only the parked module and the glossary's history note.' No DoD line asserts the ledger or rulings block remain.

findings.title: C11 consumes R24 and FR-S1's result-shape note but does not grade a transition note
findings.body: Spec B FR-S1.6 requires the release note's transition note to cover the result shape as well as the entry surface. FR-S1.7 lists that note as part of the price C11 carries. R24 names C10 and C11 as the transition-note consumers. C10's DoD lists dropped/renamed/required arguments. C12's DoD names the receipt-shape change. C11 quotes R24 and R8, and its What never mentions a transition note; its DoD grades schema validation, the cursor trial, the probe, scrub, the journal's channel field, and the two-proposal tripwire. A vet can merge C11 with no consumer-visible result-shape announcement. The priced-benefit adapters and restated progress signals are in What and likewise have no DoD bullet.
findings.suggestion: Add DoD: the same release transition note that C10/C12 write lists the native-channel result-shape change (and which engines moved). Add a recorded check that output/completion adapters and progress signals are restated against the native channel for each engine that moved.
findings.evidence: Spec B FR-S1.6: 'the release note's transition note covers the result shape as well as the entry surface.' R24 consumers: 'C10 and C11 (the transition note)'. C11.md DoD lines 6–13 have no transition-note bullet.

findings.title: C6 omits the bash-timeout log line Spec A FR-F2 assigns to this child
findings.body: Spec A FR-F2.3: 'The bash-timeout hook gets a log line at the keep-or-retire rollout child and a citation-based condition; without the log line it would be unmeasured, which is not a retirement.' C6 is that rollout child. Neither What nor DoD names the hook, the log line, or that citation-based condition. The coverage map parks the whole FR-F2.3 bullet on C5, whose body also does not mention bash-timeout. C6's census DoD allows 'unknown or unmeasured', which is the state the spec says this log line exists to prevent.
findings.suggestion: Add the log line and a citation-based keep-or-retire entry for the bash-timeout hook to C6's What and DoD. Split that sentence of FR-F2.3 to C6 on the coverage map so C5 is not the owner of a duty it does not perform.
findings.evidence: Spec A FR-F2.3 lines 1308–1310: 'The bash-timeout hook gets a log line at the keep-or-retire rollout child and a citation-based condition; without the log line it would be unmeasured, which is not a retirement.' package/coverage-map.md line 146 assigns FR-F2.3 to C5. C6.md has no 'bash-timeout' string.

findings.title: C7's reason for landing after C15 is not a DoD bullet
findings.body: R15 names C7 as consumer because 'the charters' launch and watch sections cite what remains, so C7 lands after C15'. C7's What says the showrunner launch section 'cites what orchestration remains after C15'. Sequencing after C15 is in the header. The launch DoD bullet only requires the conformance-probe preflight step, the owner's choice on a failed probe, and pointers at the dispatch-mechanics doc. A vet can pass C7 while launch/watch sections still describe detached spawn, wave-watch arming, transcript-mtime liveness, or quota. That is the outcome R15 sequenced C7 to prevent.
findings.suggestion: Add a DoD bullet: launch and watch sections name only the orchestration that remains after C15, with the PR body listing each R15 piece as cited-as-remaining or absent, matching C15's receipt outcomes.
findings.evidence: R15 consumers: 'C7 (the charters' launch and watch sections cite what remains, so C7 lands after C15)'. C7.md line 8: 'the showrunner charter's launch section names the conformance-probe preflight step and the owner's choice on a failed probe, each pointing at the dispatch-mechanics doc for the mechanism.'
